title: IDTM Installation Description
overview: This document describes all installation steps for the IDTM (Infectious Disease Treatment Module) based on the AZF4-27 Inflatable Tent system. The IDTM consists of 3 tents (2 patient pods + 1 staff pod) with 6 vestibules, hard flooring, and sun shadowing nets.

requirements.title: Safety and Security Warnings
content: Weather conditions for installation: The tent should under no circumstances be installed under wind speeds higher than 40km/h. In case of higher wind speeds, please make sure all components are safely packed and stored, away from external high winds.
Snow load (max): The tent is designed and tested for snow loads of up to 15 kg/sqm. Nevertheless, major snow loads should be removed immediately, with a telescopic snow brush if available.

Wind load (max): The tent is designed for wind speeds of up to 100 km/h (120 km/h gusts). However, such wind resistance is only possible if the tent has been installed and anchored correctly, and that the following measures are implemented as soon as wind speeds reach 40km/h: • Close all openings such as doors, windows, HVAC duct and cable sleeves. • Check that the ground is able to hold the loads and that the pegs are correctly anchored. • Replace all damaged pegs with new ones. • Make sure all furnishings inside are placed at an adequate distance from the walls and roof of the tent, as they can damage or destroy the tent cover through abrasion. Remember the wind will push the tent to the downwind side. • Outside the tent, store away all objects that may fly away, touch the tent or be touched by it.

Rain: The impact of rain on the tent itself is negligible, but the selection of the installation site has a big influence on the usability in rain. The tent cover and groundsheet are fully water-tight, but some measures can be taken to help prevent the tent from sinking into mud in case of heavy rains: • Make sure the tent is installed on an elevated area and not in a dent where the water can accumulate. • Do not build up the tent close to rivers or in dry riverbeds where flooding can occur. • Prevent the water from running under the tent by digging a drainage trench around it. Make sure the pegs can still fix the tent to the ground.

Temperature changes: Temperature changes can affect the pressure inside the inflatable frame. • Check regularly that the system is sufficiently pressurized, and re-inflate the tent once or twice a week. • Get an inflator with automatic pressure maintenance if temperature changes (day/night) occur regularly in your geographical area. In the event of condensation inside the tent, remember to open the windows to ventilate the tent, or use a suitable air-conditioning unit.

sections.title: Installation Site Selection and Preparation
sections.description: Site assessment and preparation procedures to prolong the life span of AZF Tents and improve operations

steps.title: Site Assessment
steps.purpose: Ensure optimal stability and longevity of the tent system
actions: Verify the installation site is flat to provide optimal stability for the tent and its furnishings (maximum slope: 5%)
Check for minimum surface area of 276 m² required to install the IDTM
Ensure site is at least 2m away from nearest trees or buildings
Verify ground surface is compact and dry enough to provide sufficient grip for the pegs
Measure the space needed for installation including a safety perimeter all around the designated installation area

steps.title: Site Preparation
steps.purpose: Prevent damage to tent materials and ensure proper drainage
actions: Clean the area - The installation site should be clean and free from sharp objects such as stones, chippings, branches, etc. to avoid damages to the tent groundsheet
Fill deep recesses prior to installation if slope exceeds 5%
Dig a water drainage trench around the tent installation perimeter to prevent water from sipping under the tent groundsheet in case of heavy rainfall
Keep the inside of the tent as clean as possible - Little stones, loose chippings and other peaky objects will damage the tent flooring
warnings: During installation, avoid dragging the tent components over the ground to avoid damage
Never pull with too much force, otherwise the tent's fabric will be damaged. If something cannot be moved, find a different method or get more manpower

actions: Locate the inflation valves on the lower end of each pneumatic arch, on one side of the tent, beneath the protective flaps
The inflation valve is located above the over-pressure valve
Each pneumatic arch is fitted with an inflation valve and all valves need to be connected to the electric inflator for simultaneous inflation

steps.title: Install Sun Shadowing Nets
steps.purpose: Install sun protection nets on tents

images.description: Install the 3 sun shadowing nets on the 3 tents
Install the pneumatic spacers on the roof
Spread out the 3 sun shadowing nets over tent and pneumatic spacers
Fold over the other half of the 3 sun shadowing nets completely

actions: Install the 3 sun shadowing nets on the 3 tents

Install the pneumatic spacers on the roof. Fix them lengthwise on the tent using the couplings located at the eaves and ridge of the tent. Connect the double stud on the spacer to the single stud on the tent by using a locking pin / bolt
Inflate the pneumatic spacers until the operating pressure of 0.3 bar is reached
Spread out the 3 sun shadowing nets over tent and pneumatic spacers. Fold it in half lengthwise. Align the centre line of the sun roof on the central spacer
Fold over the other half of the 3 sun shadowing nets completely, taking care to spread out the guy ropes to the outside

steps.title: Position Electric Inflator and Insert Manifold
steps.purpose: Position inflator and connect inflation hose manifold

images.description: Place the electric inflator at approximately 1 m from one tent, next to the inflation valves. Insert the inflation hose manifold inside the 'OUTLET' coupling.

actions: Place the electric inflator at approximately 1 m from one tent, next to the inflation valves
Insert the inflation hose manifold inside the 'OUTLET' coupling

steps.title: Secure Manifold with Fastening Pin
actions: Secure the manifold using the provided fastening pin

steps.title: Remove protective caps
actions: Remove the protective cap of the inflation valves by turning it counterclockwise.

steps.title: Prepare Valves for Inflation
steps.purpose: Ensure valves are properly closed before inflation
actions: Close all open valves by: pushing central pin DOWN and turning valve tappet CLOCKWISE
Check that all valves are closed. When the valve is closed, the central spring pin is up, at approximately 1 cm below the rim of the valve body.

steps.title: Connect Inflation Hoses
steps.purpose: Establish air connection to tent frame
actions: Connect end of inflation hoses to valves
Fasten hoses by turning screw ring clockwise
Ensure inflation tap is OPEN
Verify all valves are connected to inflation hoses

steps.title: Inflate Tents
steps.purpose: Erect tent structure to operating pressure

images.description: Inflator ON, tent inflating

actions: Connect the inflator to a power source and switch it on. The pneumatic frame automatically inflates.
Check that all valves are connected to an inflation hose.
We recommend you to open the doors and pull on the gable guy ropes during inflation, to facilitate the tent erection process and to prevent damages on the air passage valves of the tent.
If the inflator you are using has too many hoses, we recommend you close the tap of the unused hoses for a more efficient inflation.

steps.title: Finishing inflation

images.description: Inflator OFF

actions: Once the working pressure of 0.3 bar is reached, you can turn the inflator off.

If your inflator isn’t fitted with a pressure indicator screen, you can use the sound of the inflator as a pressure indicator. When the sound of the inflator becomes higher, wait for approximately 1 minute and turn the inflator off.

The maximum pressure of the electric inflator is 0.45 bar, which is well below the opening threshold of the pressure relief valves. This is why the over-pressure valves generally don’t open during the filling process.
Do not wait for the overpressure valves to open before switching off the inflator, as this may lead to overheating.

steps.title: Disconnect and Secure Valves

images.description: Disconnecting inflation hoses

actions: Unfasten inflation hoses from tent valves
Screw protective caps back on (turn clockwise)
Close PVC flaps to protect valves from sand/mud

steps.title: Checklist of inflation
actions: ☐ Check that the inflation manifold is inserted in the OUTLET coupling.
☐ Check that the inflation hoses are all connected to the tent valves.
☐ Check that the inflation taps are all open.
☐ Check that the inflator is connected to a power source.
☐ Check that the inflator is turned off.

steps.title: Install Pressure Feedback
actions: Locate the white pressure feedback tube inside the inflator bag, and insert the free end (with no inflation tap) in the pressure monitoring coupling of the inflator.

steps.title: Install Pressure Feedback 2
actions: Unroll the pressure feeding tube and insert the other end (with a tap) inside the tent.
You can use the HVAC duct sleeves to insert the pressure feeding tube inside the tent, or slide it through the openings of the inflation valves, as shown.

steps.title: Install Pressure Feedback 3
actions: Inside the tent, locate the pressure feedback valve on the rear pneumatic arch and open the protective cap.
You many need to disconnect the inner liner sections if an inner liner is installed.

steps.title: Install Pressure Feedback 4
actions: Insert the inflation tap inside the pressure feedback valve, fasten the screw ring, and open the tap

steps.title: Install Pressure Feedback 4
actions: Once the feedback tube is connected to the arch inside the tent, you can turn the inflator on AUTO. The current pressure inside the tent frame is displayed on the pressure control screen, and the inflator automatically turns on if the pressure is too low (below 0.2 bar).

The inflator should never be switched on AUTO if the feedback tube is not connected to the tent frame, as the inflator will be detecting an incorrect pressure level and turn on repeatedly, until it overheats.

In case of a power outage, the inflator needs to be turned OFF, and all the hose taps should be closed immediately, to prevent the air inside the frame from escaping through the inflator, which is not air-tight.

steps.title: Final Tent Positioning
actions: Pull on four corners of all 3 tents
Straighten groundsheet
Avoid folds inside tent
